answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, with total bidding capacity proportional to bonded funds. Agents such as zephyr, ripple, and falcon gain no extra capacity by splitting into aliases: every new identity needs its own bond. An attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere for a month.
